Schmidt Institute of Physics of the Earth, Russian Academy of Sciences valia@borok.yar.ru The evolution of the Earth's magnetic field at various stages of its geological history is a fundamental problem in geophysics. In particular, the question of when the Earth's solid core (ICN) was formed remains among the most complex and debated topic. According to modern geodynamo theories, after the formation of the solid core, the geomagnetic field begins to be additionally supported by compositional convection, which is more effective than the thermal one. Consequently, it is assumed that the formation of the inner solid core should be accompanied by a sharp increase in magnetic field strength. With this idea in mind, [1] suggested that an analysis of the set of experimental palaeointensity measurements (Banc ) presented in the international databases (IDBs) could serve as an independent method for estimating the formation time of the ICN. Another fundamental problem in geophysics is the geometry of the ancient geomagnetic field. Paleomagnetic reconstructions of positions of continents and crustal blocks rely on the geocentric axial dipole (GAD) hypothesis. The GAD hypothesis has been tested primarily using data on paleomagnetic field directions. Bauman Moscow State Technical University (National Research University) 3 Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute, Saint-Petersburg, Russia dm.trofimov@gmail.com The state of the ionosphere and understanding of the processes occurring in it are important for many practical applications, including satellite navigation. The delay of the navigation signal in the ionosphere is one of the main errors that affect the determination of coordinates. This problem is solved by transmitting the signal at two frequencies, which allows for the full consideration of this effect. However, the majority of GNSS equipment consists of single-frequency receivers, which do not allow for the full consideration of the ionospheric delay. The ionospheric delay is taken into account by using an ionosphere model, the parameters of which are included in the navigation signal. For GLONASS frequency-division signals, such a model is not available, which makes it necessary to create an ionosphere model that estimates the ionospheric delay based on the time and location of observations. The main characteristic of the ionosphere that affects the propagation of the navigation signal is the total electron content (TEC) of the ionosphere, which is the number of free electrons and ions in a cylinder with a cross-section of 1 m² and oriented along the line of sight. Schmidt Institute of Physics of the Earth, Russian Academy of Sciences goev@idg.ras.ru Mantle transition zone (MTZ), occurring at depths of approximately 410 and 660 km, is the region where olivine transforms into its denser states upon reaching specific P-T conditions. Accordingly, the boundaries at which these transitions occur are characterized by a sharp increase in seismic velocities. It has been established that when these boundaries interact with a cold slab (for example, in the Kuril-Kamchatka zone), their depths can vary significantly. One of the most effective tools for studying the local characteristics of these boundaries is the analysis of Ps converted waves (the PRF method). However, to achieve reliable results, it is necessary to analyze long-term records of broadband seismic data. For this reason, detailed studies of the depths of these boundaries in the Russian Far East zone were practically absent. In recent decades, the seismic networks of the Kamchatka and Sakhalin branches of the GS RAS have developed significantly, and now it compose more than 50 broadband seismometers. Processing of this data has, for the first time, made it possible to estimate the local relief of the 410 and 660 km discontinuities in the Russian Far East zone. content_preview: GC2026-SGG049 Geomechanical effects of cyclic impact on the bottomhole formation zone in laboratory conditions Zakhar Ivanov1 1 Perm National Research Polytechnic University zakhar.ivanov.2013@gmail.com The bottomhole formation zone (BFZ) is a key element of the "reservoir – well" system, determining the productivity of producing wells. During operation, the filtration characteristics of the BFZ deteriorate due to colmatation and mechanical deformations. Traditional treatment methods are often expensive and not always effective, especially in poorly consolidated reservoirs. Cyclic impact is considered a promising method for controlling filtration processes, based on creating alternating pressure gradients by periodically opening and closing the well. The geomechanical essence of the method lies in the fact that a sharp drawdown creates high pressure gradients, causing elastic deformations of the porous matrix and the destruction of colmatating deposits. content_preview: GC2026-STP071 Ion Beam Formation and Its Statistical Cooling via the Hall Electric Field in Collisionless Magnetic Reconnection Dahua Zhong1 , Andrey V. Divin1 , Igor P. Paramonik1 , Vladimir S. Semenov1 1 St Petersburg University st112995@student.spbu.ru During collisionless magnetic reconnection, decoupling of ion and electron motions establishes a multi-scale diffusion region. The ion diffusion region (IDR) embeds the smaller electron diffusion region (EDR), giving rise to the Hall current system and the associated Hall electric field [1-6]. This field efficiently accelerates ions near the diffusion region and separatrices, particularly in regimes with cold ions [7-8], significantly deforming their velocity distribution function (VDF). Using 2.5D full kinetic "Particle-in-Cell" simulations, we investigate the evolution of the ion VDF as it passes through the effective acceleration regions: the diffusion region and the separatrix. Upon rapid crossing of these regions, we observe that the accelerated particle distributions become narrower. This narrowing can be explained by a simple energy model involving the instantaneous addition of directed kinetic energy to each particle. Thus, when crossing the acceleration regions (the diffusion region and the separatrices), we observe statistical cooling of ions compared to the temperature in the inflow region. Using test particle numerical simulations, we reproduce the configuration of the electric and magnetic fields and the characteristic particle behavior when crossing the acceleration regions. The simulation results confirm that acceleration by a localized electric field can reduce the velocity spread in a particle ensemble.

content_preview: GC2026-STP072 Inferring exoplanet radius from hydrodynamic escape signatures: the role of critical atmospheric levels and stellar EUV flux Kseniia Gorbunova1 1 Institute of Computational Modeling, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences gorbunova.kd@icm.krasn.ru A significant fraction of recently discovered exoplanets remains poorly characterized: many objects lack radius or mass values. This severely limits the application of atmospheric models, the assessment of evolutionary scenarios, and creates difficulties in estimating hydrodynamic escape. In this work, we present an approach that partially overcomes this limitation: under the assumption that a planet possesses a hydrogen-dominated envelope undergoing hydrodynamic escape, numerical modeling of the atmospheric structure – including determination of the exobase and sonic point positions – enables estimation of the planetary radius from observational signatures of atmospheric loss. When observations indicate the presence of an extended hydrogen exosphere (detectable, for example, via transit spectroscopy), calculating these critical atmospheric levels provides constraints on the planet's radius. In addition to the uncertainty of the physical parameters of the planets, a significant limitation for atmospheric modeling is the lack of data on the high-energy radiation of the parent stars. A critical parameter is the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) flux, which determines the heating of the upper atmosphere and initiates a hydrodynamic escape. In this work we estimate the JEUV flux [1], [2] for the recently discovered exoplanet Gliese 251c, an Earth￾type object in the potential habitability zone at a distance of 20 li

content_preview: GC2026-STP073 Space weather phenomena observed in experiments on Cubesats of the MSU “Sozvezdie 270” during the heliogeophysical disturbances in 2025-2026 Andrey V. Bogomolov1 , Vitaliy V. Bogomolov1 , Valery E. Eremeev1 , Anatoly F. Iyudin1 , Irina N. Myagkova1 , Vladislav I. Osedlo1 , Sergey I. Svertilov1 1 Lomonosov Moscow State University aabboogg@srd.sinp.msu.ru At present Lomonosov Moscow State University (MSU) has been implementing its own space program, which observes particle fluxes in near-Earth space and electromagnetic transients of various natures, including hard X￾ray and gamma radiation from solar flares. Part of this program is the "Sozvezdie-270" project for the deployment of a constellation of CubeSat nanosatellites. This paper uses data from five CubeSats operating in a near-Earth polar orbit at an altitude of ~500 km since June 27, 2023 (Avion, Monitor-2, Monitor-3, Monitor-4, UTMN2) and data from two CubeSats operating in a similar orbit since November 5, 2024 (Altair, ArcticSat). Each of them is equipped with scintillation detectors of hard X-ray and gamma radiation as well as charged particles, specially developed at the MSU Skobeltsyn Institute of Nuclear Physics (SINP MSU) for such experiments. Data from the MSU CubeSats is available on the SINP MSU space weather website at https://swx.sinp.msu.ru/tools/davisat.php in the form of graphs and tables of monitoring data with a time resolution of up to 1 second. The MSU CubeSats observed hard X-rays >30 keV from more than 40 solar flares, primarily those of soft X-ray emission classes M and X, although weaker events were also observed. A catalog of flares is also available on the SINP MSU space weather

content_preview: GC2026-PERM041 The first results of the separation of magnetite and pyrrhotite in banded iron formation of the Kostomuksha greenstone belt of the Karelian craton based on petromagnetic data Timur R. Zaripov1 , Natalia V. Lubnina1 1 Lomonosov Moscow State University zaripov.tim000zaripov@yandex.ru Magnetite and pyrrhotite are the main magnetization-bearing minerals in banded iron formation (BIF) of the Kostomuksha Greenstone Belt (KGB) of the Karelian craton. The separation of the contribution of these minerals to the total magnetization is key to the correct calculation of the extracted iron ore, excluding the magnetization introduced by pyrrhotite. This paper presents the first results of the separation of magnetite and pyrrhotite based on thermomagnetic analysis, magnetic cleaning, and measurement of magnetic susceptibility anisotropy (AMS). Thermomagnetic analysis was performed for all types of BIF found in KGB. In all the samples studied, magnetite and pyrrhotite are distinguished by their characteristic peaks and declines in magnetic susceptibility. So the Curie point (Tc) of magnetite is 575℃, Tc of monoclinic pyrrhotite is 325℃. Pyrite (Tc = 450℃) and hematite (Tc = 680℃) are also isolated in BIF-3, while only hematite is isolated in BIF-4. A large role in the magnetization is played by multi-domain magnetite grains, which are also isolated in all samples. During heating and cooling, phase transitions and transformations of some minerals into others are recorded, which is reflected in detail in our work. As a result of the temperature demagnetization, a stable component is released in samples containing pyrrhotite (and pyrite for BIF-3) up to a temperature of 320°C

content_preview: kimo2026-main253 Позиция Германии в период восточного кризиса 1875-1878 гг. Алексей М. Ипатов1 1 Воронежский государственный педагогический университет, гуманитарный факультет, кафедра истории России, доцент, Воронеж, Россия, Россия molot.tora@mail.ru Несмотря на то, что Германия не была непосредственно вовлечена в перипетии Восточного кризиса 1875- 1878 гг., его исход, однако, мог повлиять на национальные интересы империи Гогенцоллернов. Имперский канцлер Бисмарк утверждал, что не собирается рисковать германскими гренадерами ради разрешения противоречий на Балканах. Однако германский капитал и военно-политические круги имели в данном регионе свои серьезные интересы, поэтому полностью игнорировать сложившуюся обстановку в Берлине не могли. Стремление выступить в качестве третейского судьи в противоречиях между Австро-Венгрией и Россией и, тем самым, заставить обоих союзников нуждаться еще сильнее в германской "дружбе", было лейтмотивом внешнеполитической стратегии Бисмарка и его соратников в эти годы. Ряд исследователей и вовсе видели в официальной германской позиции стремление отомстить России за ее "спасение" Франции в ходе "военной тревоги" 1875 г. Проникновение" Германии в Турцию произошло уже в 1880-е гг., однако уже ранее наблюдались периодические контакты в военной и экономической отраслях. Ключевым моментом признания активной роли Берлина в Восточном кризисе явилось избрание германской столицы местом проведения международного конгресса по итогам русско-турецкой войны 1877-1878 гг. Для отечественной исторической науки особенно чувствительным моментом, вызывающим дискуссии в историографии, представляется позиция Бисмарка в отношении России в июне-июле 1878 г. Спектр
